title: Fingerstick a trainer hand: twist the lancet's tab off, hold the ring finger still, fire square, discard in sharps
instruction: A fingerstick trainer lies palm up on a board clamped to the table: a palm block with an index finger, a thumb and a ring finger, its fingertips lowered; the ring finger rides on a light spring and gives way when pressed unless it is held. A BD Microtainer contact-activated lancet (21 G x 1.8 mm) stands tip down in a stand whose socket holds its protective tab, and a BD sharps container stands beside. Do a fingerstick as BD directs. Done means: the lancet's tab was twisted off in the stand before the lancet came out of it; the ring finger was held still by a gripper closed on it from the lancet's first touch until after it fired; the lancet fired square to the skin on a side of the ring fingertip's pad, without sliding; and the used lancet is inside the sharps container, let go.
context: O*NET Core tasks (relevant to at least 67% of incumbents): Phlebotomists 31-9097.00 (Employment (2025) 143,900), "Draw blood from capillaries by dermal puncture, such as heel or finger stick methods."; Medical Assistants 31-9092.00 (833,900), "Collect blood, tissue, or other laboratory specimens, log the specimens, and prepare them for testing." The CMA (AAMA) exam outline lists "Capillary/Dermal puncture (finger, heel, ear)"; NCCT's medical assistant plan, "Perform capillary punctures (i.e., fingerstick, heelstick)." BD's guide: "Twist off the tab"; "press safety lancet firmly against the puncture site." A hospital laboratory procedure for this lancet's family: "Grasp the finger, and using a sterile lancet, press firmly against the finger to make a puncture." The skill: one hand holds the punctured finger still while the other fires a sharp square on its curved tip.
setup: Coordinates: x forward from the arm bases (at y +-0.305), y left, z up from the table top. Fixed: a stand (40 mm square, 25 mm high, printed) at (0.34, -0.2): a fixed post holds the lancet's tab cap and a cup on it, keyed to the lancet's front (13.8 x 10.8 mm pocket, 8 mm deep), turns up to 100 deg either way; the tab breaks off when the lancet is turned 45 deg either way, against 3 N-cm (rig.scad, parts stand and cup). A BD 305635 sharps container (124.5 x 109.2 x 165.1 mm), centred at (0.22, -0.36), its lid opening 63.5 x 30.5 mm. The stand and the container are taped to the table. Loose: a BD Microtainer contact-activated lancet 366577 (21 G x 1.8 mm, pink), modelled as a 13 x 10 x 37 mm polypropylene housing (4 g) and a 7 mm contact shield standing 3 mm proud on a spring (4 N/mm, 1 N preload); it fires at 8 N on the shield (1.75 mm of travel). It stands tip down in the cup. A fingerstick trainer (printed PETG, rig.scad) lies palm up on a 6 mm plywood board: a plate under the hand and a bar running back between the arm bases, held to the table by two C-clamps on the bar (fixed in the sim). On the board a post carries a palm block with an index finger and a thumb, fixed, and a ring finger (life size, tip radius 7.3 mm, 25 g, a Wallcur Lance trainer finger sleeve, REM-LANCE-KIT-01D, over its distal pad, its material unpublished) on a vertical linear guide behind its knuckle: two springs (0.1 N/mm in all) hold it up on a top stop with 1 N to spare over its weight, so a downward push of 1.20 N moves it 2 mm, and it stops 10 mm down. No middle or little finger. The fingers slope down 20 deg from the knuckles to the tips; the ring's apex (on its axis) at (0.26, -0.12) and 100 mm over the table, the fingers pointing +x, away from the arm bases, the thumb toward -y (before the seed's shift). The base is shifted in x and in y each uniform within +-12 mm and turned uniform within +-6 deg about a point 140 mm behind the ring's apex, level along the hand (the palm's middle), drawn from the trial's seed; the board and its clamps are placed to match.
scoring: The site: either side of the ring fingertip's pad, 8 to 15 mm back from the apex and 15 to 60 deg round from the pad's middle line; the shield's face within 1.5 mm of the skin is on it. Square: the lancet's axis within 10 deg of the skin's local normal where it touches. A slide: the face moving more than 1 mm on the skin between first touch and firing; lifting off ends a placement. The touch: the shield's face within 0.3 mm of the ring finger's skin, or the shield off its stop with its face on the ring finger; a touch on the table or another finger does not count. Held: a gripper closed on the ring finger, its finger half-gap 6.4 to 8.2 mm (from 1.5 mm under to 0.3 mm over the 7.9 mm it reads closed on the finger; wider, the pads are off the skin), whether or not it also counts as holding the lancet, its TCP within 15 mm of the finger's axis between its distal joint and its base and at most 4 mm off the axis along its closing direction, its pad tips past the axis; it must hold at every step from the lancet's first touch until 0.5 s after the click. Still: the ring finger pushed at most 2 mm down, read at its slide and at its fingertip, over the same window. Out of the stand: the lancet moved more than 4 mm across or 10 mm up from where it stood; once out it stays out, so a lancet put back in the stand and let go is a drop. Rungs, at the last step (0 once any fault has latched; the fire counts once reached): 0.25 the tab twisted off and the lancet out of the stand; 0.5 and fired square on the site, the ring finger held and still from the touch, without a slide; 0.75 and the used lancet inside the sharps container, let go by both hands; 1.0 that held 1 s. No rung for a placement without a fire: a real trial reads the site and the square at the click. Scored 0 from then on: the lancet lifted out with its tab on; the lancet fired in the stand (tab off, pressed down on the post); the ring finger not still; a step without the hold from first touch to 0.5 s after the click; a fire with no gripper holding the ring finger; a slide; a fire off the site or tilted; the lancet, once out of the stand, held by neither gripper and outside the container for 0.5 s (dropped; held: a gripper's finger half-gap 3 to 7 mm, so closed on either side of the housing, and its TCP within 15 mm of the lancet's axis from 10 mm beyond its face to 53 mm up it; let go: a gripper's half-gap over 7 mm or its TCP over 60 mm from that axis); the trainer's base 5 mm or 2 deg off its layout pose (it is clamped; this checks that the sim placed it); the lancet 30 mm under the table top; the firing model not running. Real trials (README) read the touch as the first 60 fps side-camera frame where the shield meets the ring finger, the stillness on the side camera, scaled by steel rules filmed beside the web and the fingertip before the arms go live, the hold on the cameras and the arm's log, the click on audio, the discard on the overhead video and a 0.01 g scale.
reset_notes: A new lancet in the cup each trial (a used one is spent; its tab stays in the post's slot and is removed); the ring finger back on its top stop; the base placed by seed; the container emptied of the trial's lancet.
fidelity: Approximate. The lancet's drive is a sprung shield that fires at a set force; needle, puncture and blood are not simulated. The tab is a sprung turn that breaks at 45 deg either way. A real finger's give at its joints, wrist and arm is one vertical sprung slide behind its knuckle. The base is fixed (clamped in the rig). The lancet's size, fire force, tab torque and the slide's spring are estimates, measured before trials; the hold's 7.9 mm on-finger half-gap is checked on the film.
scores: Dream-1 run: 0 (1,200 steps); demo: 1.0 (success at 40.05 s, step 801)
